# 1 Clement Chapter 5 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalence)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 5 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/1CL_005_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 5

**[TRANSLATOR'S NOTE: Chapter 5 is the earliest extrabiblical witness to the martyrdoms of Peter and Paul. Written c. 96 CE from Rome, it confirms both apostles died in Rome, and that Paul traveled to Spain ("the extreme limit of the West"). The Greek root martys/martyrion underlies "testimony/witness" — the martyrdom vocabulary is nascent here.]**

**5:1** But let us set aside examples of ancient times and come to the athletes who were nearest to our own day. Let us take the noble examples of our own generation.

**5:2** Because of jealousy and envy the greatest and most righteous pillars were persecuted and contended to the death.

**5:3** Let us set before our eyes the good apostles.

**5:4** Peter, who because of unrighteous jealousy endured not one or two but many trials, and having thus borne his witness went to the place of glory that was his due.

**5:5** Because of jealousy and contention Paul demonstrated the prize of endurance:

**5:6** Seven times he bore chains; he was exiled; he was stoned; he served as a herald in both the East and the West; he attained noble fame through his faith;

**5:7** And having taught righteousness to the whole world, and having reached the farthest limit of the West, and having given his testimony before rulers, he thus departed from the world and was taken up into the holy place — having become the most outstanding pattern of endurance.

---

*LOGOS renders with careful attention to the martyrdom vocabulary. "Borne his witness" preserves the martys root.*
